items.title: This Photographer Shows What Iceland’s Glacial Rivers Look Like From Above, And It’s Breathtaking (20 Pics)
items.summary:
At first glance, Radoslav Sviretsov’s photos could pass for abstract paintings, or even for something seen under a microscope. Thin threads of turquoise branch across black backgrounds, white mineral crusts swirl around pools of electric blue, and streaks of gold run through fields of gray. But every image shows a real place in Iceland, captured from above at a single moment in a landscape that never stops changing.

Sviretsov is an architect and photographer based in Reykjavík. His ongoing series, "The Shape of Water", follows the element that has done more than any other to shape the island. Here water takes almost every form imaginable. It sits frozen inside ancient glaciers, rushes through vast braided rivers, rises as steam from geothermal springs and seeps through volcanic ground. Wherever it moves, it rewrites the land, carving channels, carrying sediment and leaving behind layers of minerals.

More info: sviretsov.com | Instagram 

#1 The Heart Of Iceland Deep in the mountains of Iceland lies this hidden paradise lake, surrounded by the softest and brightest green moss on the planet. Untouched by human feet. Just as it should remain.

© Photo: Radoslav Sviretsov 

Being an architect plays a big part in how Sviretsov approaches the landscape. “As an architect, I’m drawn to natural geometry,” the Reykjavík-based photographer explained in the interview with Bored Panda . Shooting mostly from directly above, the series leaves out the horizon, the sky and every other clue that would make these scenes read as ordinary landscapes. What remains is pure composition: lines,…

items.title: 41 Crochet Masterpieces That Show What Happens When Creativity Meets A Hook And Yarn (New Pics)
items.summary:
For a long time, crochet had a certain reputation: lace doilies on a side table, granny-square blankets, and a slow pastime for quiet evenings. That picture is now badly out of date. Today's makers use nothing more than a hook and a ball of yarn to create lifelike animals, wearable art, intricate lace, and sculptural pieces that would look more at home in a gallery than in a sewing basket. 

Part of what makes the craft so remarkable is that every crocheted piece is made entirely by hand. Knitting has been done by machine for centuries, but no machine has ever fully replicated crochet stitches. That means every item in this list was built one loop at a time, often over many hours, days, or even weeks of work. 

Scroll down to see 41 crochet creations that show just how far the craft has come, and upvote your favorites along the way. 

#1 Finally Finished My Tradescantia Zebrina © Photo: 666Skittles 

The craft itself is younger than many people assume. Its name comes from the French word "crochet," meaning "small hook," and historians generally agree it only became widespread in Europe in the early 19th century. It soon proved its value. During Ireland's Great Famine in the 1840s, crocheted lace became a vital source of income for many families, and intricate Irish crochet pieces were sold across Europe and beyond.

#2 Tomatoes On The Vine 🍅 © Photo: bugvert 

Since then, crochet has kept finding new and unexpected uses. In 1997, mathematician Daina Taimina used it to create physical models of hyperbolic space, a type of geometry that mathematicians had long struggled to…
items.t: 41 Crochet Masterpieces That Show What Happens When Creativity Meets A Hook And Yarn (New Pics)

One of Malcolm’s aunts, his mother’s sister, was a deeply Christian woman who believed Christmas was all about the birth of Christ. So, when the show opened with a “stripper Santa Claus” dressed seductively, she was shocked.

“Oh my God! This is not what Christmas is about!” she yelled.

It clearly wasn’t the Christmas show she had been expecting.

Then, another aunt, who was terrified of spiders, began frantically hitting herself because she thought she felt one crawling on her. He immediately shared that his mother was “going through something” and wasn’t listening to what she was saying. Instead, he suggested that they travel to visit Liv’s parents. He took his wife’s side, which made her happy. Meanwhile, her sister-in-law’s husband decided to follow their mother’s plan.

“Every Christmas, my mother-in-law hosts everybody at their big family vacation home in Florida. Coincidentally, it’s also like the only time of year my husband and I get to go on a vacation,” she says.

However, she says her mother-in-law called her husband and told him that the trip was only for family, with no wives allowed.

“She asks me what I’m planning on packing for Christmas vacation. I’m sorry, I was told that we weren’t invited. It was blood family only. She’s like, what do you mean? All the wives are going. Even boyfriends and girlfriends are going,” she recalls.

items.title: Woman With “One Friend on a Good Day” Worries Her Future Wedding Will Be “Practically Empty”
items.summary:
A 25-year-old woman has been thinking about her future lately. She has been dating a man for almost a year and hopes to get married someday, but the thought of planning a wedding makes her sad. Her main concern is that she is introverted and has very few friends, unlike her partner, who has a large social circle. She wondered how embarrassing it would be if she had almost no one to invite from her side of the family and friends.

The post, shared on November 15, drew 115 comments as of publication.

The woman began her post by writing that her boyfriend was extremely extroverted and had a large social circle, with tons of longtime friends. He was often invited to weddings, engagement parties and other events. The woman shared that she had attended some of these events with her boyfriend and noticed that the brides always had so many friends, including bridesmaids, large groups of girlfriends and people they had known forever.

How do people with no friends even have weddings?
